# Additional recommended reading

**Why this section exists**

These readings and websites give helpful background, examples, and visual inspiration. None are required, but all are useful if you want to go deeper.

## Papers and chapters

- Broman, K. W., & Woo, K. H. (2018). Data organization in spreadsheets. *The American Statistician*, 72(1), 2–10.
- Gotelli, N. J., & Ellison, A. M. (2013). Chapter 4, *Framing and Testing Hypotheses*, in *A Primer of Ecological Statistics* (2nd ed.). Sinauer.
- Petchey, O., Beckerman, A., & Childs, D. (2009). Shock and awe by statistical software — why R? *Bulletin of the British Ecological Society*, 40(4), 55–58.
- Weissgerber, T. L., Milic, N. M., Winham, S. J., & Garovic, V. D. (2015). Beyond bar and line graphs: time for a new data presentation paradigm. *PLoS Biology*, 13(4), e1002128. [https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.1002128](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.1002128)
- Wickham, H. (2014). Tidy data. *Journal of Statistical Software*, 59(10), 1–23.

## Useful websites

- The R Graph Gallery: [https://www.r-graph-gallery.com/](https://www.r-graph-gallery.com/)
- Datanovia ggplot2 tutorials: [https://www.datanovia.com/learn/data-visualization/ggplot2/](https://www.datanovia.com/learn/data-visualization/ggplot2/)
- Datanovia R foundations: [https://www.datanovia.com/learn/programming/r-foundations/](https://www.datanovia.com/learn/programming/r-foundations/)

**Tip:** Pick one reading and one website and spend 30 minutes exploring. A little browsing goes a long way.
